info.title: OddsRelay API
info.description:
The OddsRelay odds API: matched boards, the raw board, discovery, coverage and status, as served at `https://api.oddsrelay.io`. Every route is `GET`; a trailing slash is ignored; an unknown path is 404 `not_found`; any other method is 405 `method_not_allowed` (a `HEAD`'s 405 has no body). A request that carries a body (none is read) is answered with `Connection: close`, and its connection ends.

## Keys
Send the key as `Authorization: Bearer <key>` or `x-api-key: <key>`, never in the query string. Server keys start `or_live_`; browser and dashboard keys start `or_pub_`, answer only calls from their own website's `Origin` (else 403 `origin_not_allowed`), and get `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` echoing that exact origin (never `*`). A browser's CORS preflight (`OPTIONS` with an `Origin`) is answered 204. Keyless routes: `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/coverage` without a key header, `/v2/openapi.json`.

## Order of checks
The per-address shield (429 `too_many_from_address`), the key (401), the account's flood cap (429 `too_many_requests`), a suspended account (403 `account_suspended`; `/v2/usage` still answers), a browser key's website (403), then the route's own checks, each described on its operation. Every refusal is free.

## Tokens
One token pool per account, reset monthly; a trial's pool is one-off, so its reset is the trial's end when that comes first. A call's price comes from the request (the product and its filters), never from the reply's size: `/v2/pricing` publishes the table, `quote=true` prices any data request for free, and discovery, `/v2/usage`, `/v2/pricing`, 304s, replies with no events and every refusal are free. A price above the balance is 402 `insufficient_tokens`. Every reply to a valid key carries `X-Tokens-Cost`, plus `X-Tokens-Used`, `-Remaining`, `-Limit` and `-Reset` whenever the balance is known (`unlimited` on an unlimited account).

## Flood cap
One cap per account, per 10 seconds and per minute (dashboard keys have their own), plus a cap on requests in flight. Every reply to a valid key after authentication carries `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `-Remaining` and `-Reset` for the window with fewer left; over it is 429 `too_many_requests` with `Retry-After`. The front door also caps each address and the whole service: those 429s carry `Retry-After` and an EMPTY body with no `code`, as does its 502.

## Errors
Every JSON error is `{"error": {"code", "message", "request_id"}}`, plus `type` on a scope 403, `valid` on the four unknown-value 400s and on the four `*_not_in_plan` 403s (`bookmaker_not_in_plan`, `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `exchange_not_in_plan`: outside your plan's bookmakers or your account's scope; `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope), `products` on an `unknown_market` that another product carries (the products that carry it), the balance fields on 402 and `reason`/`dashboard_url` on `account_suspended`. Branch on `code`. `request_id` equals the reply's `X-OddsRelay-Request-Id` (a 405 carries it in the body only).

## Account scope
An account can carry a scope: per product, the sports, markets, bookmakers and exchanges it may read (raw's one `bookmakers` list names venues of both kinds). A product outside it is 403 `not_in_key_scope` for every key on the account; a value a call names outside it is 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan` or `exchange_not_in_plan` with `valid` (the scope's list for that product), `quote=true` included; a filter the call leaves out is trimmed to the scope, before the price. `GET /v2/usage` shows the scope (`scope`, `scope_version`; both null when the account has none). A scope that cannot be applied answers every data route and keyed `/v2/coverage` 503 `temporarily_unavailable`, never the unscoped data.

## Strict inputs
Each route reads the parameters listed on it; any other parameter, or one sent twice, is 400 `bad_request` naming it. `region` is one lowercase code; missing means `uk`.

## Gzip
Send `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses): bodies over 1 kB are then gzip. A request that refuses gzip (`Accept-Encoding` naming `gzip` or `x-gzip` with `q=0`, `*;q=0` with no gzip above 0, or `identity` alone: Python's `urllib` and `http.client` send `identity` unless told otherwise) gets plain bodies, but `standard`, `dutching` and raw answer it 400. A request with no `Accept-Encoding` gets plain bodies: the front door decompresses them and keeps the gzip representation's `ETag`. `/healthz`, `/v2/status`, `/v2/health`, `/v2/usage`, quotes and errors are always plain.

## Caching
Data replies (never a `quote=true` price), `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events` and `/v2/bookmakers` carry `ETag`, a label of the decompressed content; send it as `If-None-Match` and an unchanged body is 304 with no body, free. Keyed replies are `Cache-Control: private, max-age=2, must-revalidate` and `Vary: Authorization, Accept-Encoding, Origin`.

## Freshness
`meta.processed_at` and `X-Processed-At` are a board's time; `X-OddsRelay-Version` is the publish instant of the board version served (epoch ms), the same on every route for one publish; `meta.last_seen` (matched boards) and `last_seen` (keyed `/v2/coverage`) are when each venue and sport was last read; raw's `last_update` is when a venue's market last changed. The API cuts no row for age, but a venue whose latest read is older than its own window (twice its longest recurring gap between reads, at most two minutes) is left off the boards until it is read again.

## Versions
`/v2` is frozen as of 2026-09-21: from that date it takes additions only, meaning a new route, parameter, field, value or code that a client coded against `/v2` can ignore. A breaking change is anything that client cannot ignore: a route, field, value or code removed or renamed, a type or meaning changed, a new required input, or a refusal where there was an answer. A client must accept fields, values and codes it does not know. A breaking change ships only under a new path, `/v3`, announced at least 6 months ahead by email and in the changelog, and `/v2` is kept for at least 12 months after `/v3` ships. Anything scheduled to end carries `Deprecation` and `Sunset` headers on its replies. Event ids are opaque, and an event's id never changes for its fixture: once an id has been served, every later answer for that fixture carries it. If two ids turn out to be one fixture, the one served first is kept, and the other is listed in the event's `previous_ids` and still answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds`. Changing a served id is a breaking change. `X-OddsRelay-Api-Version` equals `info.version`, on every reply but `/healthz`, a `HEAD`'s 405 and the empty-bodied 429s and 502; additions never change it, and a new label comes only with a new version path.

get.description:
The six matched boards: each event's bookmaker back prices beside the exchanges' lay prices (`dutching`: back legs that cover every outcome, grouped by `dutch_id`; `each-way` and `extra-place`: each-way terms against win and place lays).

**Checks, in this order** (each refusal is free): the per-address shield, the key, the account's flood cap, a suspended account, a browser key's website, the API version; then `type` (404 `unknown_type`), `region`, the region in the key (403 `region_not_in_scope`), the product in the key (403 `not_in_key_scope`), the product in the region (403 `product_not_in_region`: a region with no exchange serves only dutching and raw); then the parameters: each one this route reads, once; `format`, `oddsFormat` and `dateFormat` values; on `standard` and `dutching` decimal ISO only and gzip accepted (400 `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`); then the filters (400 unknown values, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`, then your account's scope: 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan`, `exchange_not_in_plan`; and your plan's bookmaker list), then `quote=true`, the price (402), and the board (503 while it is not ready).

**Filters** cut the whole board's events in order: sport and kick-off, then markets, then back offers by bookmaker and lay offers by exchange; an outcome left with no back or no lay goes, then empty markets and events. `dutching` keeps a dutch only when every leg is a named venue. A filtered reply is priced on its filters (`/v2/pricing`); the kick-off window is never priced.

**Freshness**: `meta.processed_at` and `X-Processed-At` are the board time; `meta.last_seen` is each venue and sport's last read. The API drops no row for age; a venue not read within its own window (at most two minutes) is off the board until its next read.

**Conditional requests**: send the `ETag` back as `If-None-Match`; an unchanged body is a 304 with no body, free. A reply with no events is free.

get.description:
Every venue's prices per event, one page at a time: bookmakers as `{name, price}`, exchanges quoting a lay side as `{name, back_price, lay_price, available}`. Served gzip only: a request refusing gzip is 400 `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`.

**Checks, in this order**: the per-address shield, the key, the flood cap, a suspended account, a browser key's website, the API version; `region`, the region and `raw` in the key; the parameters (each one this route reads, once) and their values; the filters (400 unknown values, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`, 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan`, then your account's scope: 403 `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan`); `includeLinks` and `includeLiquidity`; `limit`; `cursor`; gzip; the raw board (503 `raw_not_enabled`); the page (503 while it cannot be cut); `quote=true`; the price (402).

**Paging**: pages are ordered by (kick-off, event id) and a cursor resumes strictly after the last event it saw, so an event that leaves the board between pages never restarts the walk. The accepted limit: an event whose kick-off moves across the cursor during a walk can appear twice or be missed. Dedupe by event `id`, and take a missed event on the next walk. A cursor expires 300 s after it was issued.

**Following changes**: walk with `updatedSince` set to the start of your previous walk; `last_update` is when a venue's market last moved (see the schema for what it is not).

**Price**: a page pays its share of the query's price (its prices over all the query's events' prices, at least 1; `eventIds` and `requireBookmakers` narrow the page, never the query), so a whole walk pays the query's price (narrowed by `eventIds` or `requireBookmakers`, only its kept events' share of it); a recent `updatedSince` pays a reduced share. `quote=true` prices this page.

text/plain.example:
ok
boards: 6/6 servable
liveness only - the feed's health verdict is /v2/health

region.name: region
region.description: ONE lowercase region code (`/v2/regions` lists yours). Missing means `uk`: on a data route only when your key covers `uk`, else 400 `region_required` naming a code your key has; on discovery and keyless routes always. A comma list, the parameter sent twice or an uppercase code is 400 `bad_request`; an unknown code, or one with no live bookmaker here, is 404 `unknown_region`.

format.name: format
format.description: `envelope` (default): `{meta, data}`. `bare`: the `data` array alone, `meta` moved to `X-*` headers.

oddsFormat.name: oddsFormat
oddsFormat.description: `decimal` (default) or `american` (a signed integer; null for a price at or below 1.0). `standard` and `dutching` serve decimal only: anything else is 400.

dateFormat.name: dateFormat
dateFormat.description: `iso` (default, ISO-8601 UTC) or `unix` (integer epoch seconds) for `commence_time`, `processed_at` and `last_update`. `standard` and `dutching` serve iso only: anything else is 400.

quote.name: quote
quote.description: `true` (also `1`, `yes`, `on`): price this exact request instead of serving it. 200 `{cost, remaining, rate_card}`, free, every check before the price still applies; any other value is an ordinary request.

sports.name: sports
sports.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: a sport key or a prefix of one as `/v2/sports` lists them (`horse_racing`, `soccer`), lowercased. A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Unknown is 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid` (the sport key bases). A known value with nothing on the board is an empty 200, free. A value is inside your account's scope when it starts with a scope sport (every `soccer_…` key under `soccer`); outside, 403 `sport_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

bookmakers.name: bookmakers
bookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: bookmaker keys as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them (a listed name is accepted too). Unknown is 400 `unknown_bookmaker` with `valid`; an exchange here is that 400 naming `exchanges` (on `dutching` both lists take venues of either kind); a venue outside the region is 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`; one outside your plan's bookmaker list or your account's scope is 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan` with `valid` (on `dutching`, an exchange outside the scope is 403 `exchange_not_in_plan`). A plan with a bookmaker list, or an account scope, trims a call naming none to that list.

exchanges.name: exchanges
exchanges.description: Comma-separated, at most 4: exchange keys as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them. Unknown is 400 `unknown_exchange` with `valid`; a bookmaker here is that 400 naming `bookmakers`. Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `exchange_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

markets.name: markets
markets.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: market keys (`h2h`, `totals`, …; `/v2/sports` rows list the keys seen under each competition). Each product's keys: keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets`. Unknown is 400 `unknown_market` with `valid` (this product's keys) and, when another product carries it, `products`; another product's key may instead be accepted and match nothing. Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `market_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

commenceTimeFrom.name: commenceTimeFrom
commenceTimeFrom.description: Events kicking off at or after this ISO-8601 instant (no offset = UTC; a fraction of a second rounds up). Not ISO-8601 is 400; on the matched boards a From after To is 400.

commenceTimeTo.name: commenceTimeTo
commenceTimeTo.description: Events kicking off at or before this ISO-8601 instant (no offset = UTC).

rawSports.name: sports
rawSports.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: a sport key, a prefix of one, or a sport name raw serves, lowercased. A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Unknown is 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid`. Inside your account's raw scope: a key or prefix starting with a scope sport, a sport name only when it equals one (send `soccer`, not `football`); outside, 403 `sport_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

rawSport.name: sport
rawSport.description: The same as `sports` (what `/v2/events` takes); ignored when `sports` is sent.

leagues.name: leagues
leagues.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: competition names (an event's league or `sport_title`), lowercased. Not checked against a catalogue.

rawBookmakers.name: bookmakers
rawBookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40: venue keys of either kind, bookmakers and exchanges, as `/v2/bookmakers` lists them. Unknown is 400 `unknown_bookmaker` with `valid`; outside the region 403 `bookmaker_not_in_region`; outside your plan's bookmaker list or your account's raw scope 403 `bookmaker_not_in_plan` with `valid`. An account scope's raw list is the whole venue list, exchanges included: left out, trimmed to it (so `exchangesOnly=true` keeps only the exchanges it names).

rawRequireBookmakers.name: requireBookmakers
rawRequireBookmakers.description: Comma-separated, at most 40 venue keys, checked as `bookmakers` is (the same 400 and 403 codes). Keeps only the events where EVERY named venue quotes the call's `markets` (with several, at least one of them each), under `exchangesOnly` if set; a venue that lists the event but not the market does not count. `bookmakers` does not narrow this test and `updatedSince` is not part of it: with `updatedSince`, an event carrying every named venue is kept when any venue shown changed, and the page shows only the venues that changed. It narrows events, never venues: every venue the other filters keep is still shown, named or not. `meta.total` and `X-Count` count the events kept. Price: like `eventIds`, it narrows the page and not the query, so a page pays its share of the same call without `requireBookmakers`, and an empty page is free.

rawMarkets.name: markets
rawMarkets.description: Comma-separated, at most 20: market keys raw serves. Raw's keys: keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets.raw`. Unknown is 400 `unknown_market` with `valid` (raw's keys) and, when another product carries it, `products`. Keeps venues quoting one of them, and only those markets. Outside your account's scope for this product: 403 `market_not_in_plan` with `valid`; left out, trimmed to the scope.

rawEventIds.name: eventIds
rawEventIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids. An id merged into another (in that event's `previous_ids`) returns that event. Narrows the page, not the query: a page pays its share of the same call without `eventIds`.

updatedSince.name: updatedSince
updatedSince.description: Exactly `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ` (any other form is 400). Keeps venues whose `last_update` is at or after it, and the events holding one. The bulk way to follow raw: a recent `updatedSince` pays a reduced share (`/v2/pricing` `recent`).

includeLinks.name: includeLinks
includeLinks.description: `true`: each venue's `link` (its primary event page; left out when it has none). Default `false`. `true` or `false`, else 400.

includeLiquidity.name: includeLiquidity
includeLiquidity.description: `false`: leave out `available` beside an exchange's `lay_price`. Default `true`. `true` or `false`, else 400.

cursor.name: cursor
cursor.description: The previous page's `meta.next_cursor` (or `X-Next-Cursor`). A cursor is bound to no account and expires 300 s after it was issued: 400 `cursor expired: start again from the first page`; any other shape 400 `cursor not recognised: start again from the first page`.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Events per page, 1-250 (default and maximum 250). Anything else is 400.

eventsSport.name: sport
eventsSport.description: Required: a sport key or a prefix of one as `/v2/sports` lists them. A competition key (an event's `competition_key`, listed on `/v2/sports`) returns every event of that competition, whatever its venues call it. Any other key returns what it returned before, plus every event a venue files under a key it begins (each venue names its league its own way), and, when every event that key has ever named belongs to ONE competition, the rest of that competition. Missing is 400 `missing_param`; unknown 400 `unknown_sport` with `valid`.

eventsEventIds.name: eventIds
eventsEventIds.description: Comma-separated, at most 50 event ids. An id merged into another (in that event's `previous_ids`) returns that event.

type.name: type
type.description: A matched board: `standard`, `2up`, `dutching`, `each-way`, `extra-place` or `bog`. The aliases `two-up`, `each_way` and `extra_place` are accepted and served as their canonical slug. Anything else is 404 `unknown_type`.

eventId.name: id
eventId.description: An event id (`or_evt_…`) from raw, a matched board or `/v2/events`. An id that was merged into another (it is in that event's `previous_ids`) answers that event, whose own id is in the body. Not on the raw board now is 404 `unknown_event`.

acceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
acceptEncoding.description: Send `gzip`; with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses the reply. `standard` and `dutching` answer a request that refuses gzip (`identity` alone, as Python's `urllib` sends by default, or `gzip;q=0` or `*;q=0`) with 400 `bad_request`, message `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`; the other four boards answer it plain.

rawAcceptEncoding.name: Accept-Encoding
rawAcceptEncoding.description: Send `gzip`; with curl, `--compressed` sends it and decompresses the reply. The raw board answers a request that refuses gzip (`identity` alone, as Python's `urllib` sends by default, or `gzip;q=0` or `*;q=0`) with 400 `bad_request`, message `add Accept-Encoding: gzip; with curl use --compressed`.

X-OddsRelay-Api-Version.description: The API version label, equal to this document's `info.version`. On every reply but `/healthz`, a `HEAD`'s 405 and the empty-bodied 429s and 502.

X-OddsRelay-Request-Id.description: This request's id (`or_req_` + 32 hex), the same value as an error body's `request_id`: quote it when you contact us. On data and discovery 200s, quotes, `/v2/usage` and `/v2/pricing` 200s and every JSON error but a 405; not on 304s, `/v2/health`, `/v2/regions`, `/v2/coverage` 200s or `/v2/odds/event/{id}` 200s.

ETag.description: The content label. Data replies (never a `quote=true` price), `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events` and `/v2/bookmakers`: `"c<CRC-32, 8 hex>-<length hex>"` of the DECOMPRESSED body, with `-gz` appended inside the quotes on the gzip representation, so it changes when, and only when, those bytes change. `/v2/pricing` and `/v2/openapi.json`: the body's SHA-256 hex, `-gz` likewise. Send it back as `If-None-Match` for a 304 (weak comparison; `*` matches any).

X-OddsRelay-Version.description: The publish instant of the board version the body was cut from, epoch milliseconds. One publish reads one value on every route that serves it. Present whenever the board version is known.

X-Processed-At.description: The board time, equal to `meta.processed_at` (ISO-8601 UTC, milliseconds). Also on 304s and on `format=bare` replies; never on a `quote=true` price.

X-Count.description: `format=bare` only: the events served (matched boards), or the rows across all pages (raw, `/v2/sports`, `/v2/events`, `/v2/bookmakers`).

X-Next-Cursor.description: `format=bare` only, raw and paged discovery: the next page's cursor, empty on the last page.

X-Tokens-Cost.description: Tokens this reply cost: 0 on a free reply (304, an empty reply, discovery, `/v2/usage`, `/v2/pricing`, a quote and every refusal). On every reply to a valid key, refusals included; never on a 401, on the per-address 429 or on a keyless route.

X-Tokens-Used.description: Tokens the account has used this period. Sent with the other balance headers whenever the balance is known (while the key registry is unreachable a reply can carry `X-Tokens-Cost` alone).

X-Tokens-Remaining.description: Tokens left this period, or `unlimited` on an unlimited account. Sent when the balance is known.

X-Tokens-Limit.description: The account's tokens for the period, or `unlimited`. Sent when the balance is known.

X-Tokens-Reset.description: When the pool resets (ISO-8601 UTC, whole seconds); on a trial, the trial's end when that comes first. Sent when the balance is known.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: The account's flood cap for the window with fewer requests left (per 10 seconds or per minute; your numbers are in `/v2/usage` `flood_cap`). On every reply to a valid key after authentication, 429 `too_many_requests` included; never on a 401, the per-address 429 or a keyless route.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying: on every 429 and 503. A 402 never carries it.

Access-Control-Allow-Origin.description: `*` on every GET reply of a keyless route (`/v2/status`, keyless `/v2/coverage`, `/v2/openapi.json`), refusals and errors included. A keyed reply never sends `*`: a browser or dashboard key's reply echoes the exact request `Origin` when the key allows it, with `Access-Control-Expose-Headers`.

Cache-Control.description: Keyed replies: `private, max-age=2, must-revalidate`. `/v2/status`: `public, max-age=10`; keyless `/v2/coverage`: `public, max-age=60`; `/v2/openapi.json`: `public, max-age=300`; `/healthz`: `no-store`.

Vary.description: Keyed replies: `Authorization, Accept-Encoding, Origin`. Keyless `/v2/coverage`: `Authorization, X-Api-Key, Accept-Encoding`. `/v2/openapi.json`: `Accept-Encoding`. JSON errors on `/v2` routes: `Origin`.

Content-Encoding.description: `gzip` when the body is gzip (see the gzip rules in the description).

ErrorBody.description: Every JSON 4xx and 5xx this API writes.

code.description: Stable machine code; branch on this, never on `message`.

type.description: Scope 403s only: which axis refused (`not_in_key_scope` and `product_not_in_region` product; `region_not_in_scope` and `bookmaker_not_in_region` region; `schema_not_in_scope` schema).

valid.description: `unknown_sport` (sport key bases), `unknown_bookmaker`, `unknown_exchange`, `bookmaker_not_in_plan` (your plan's bookmakers, or your account scope's, in the call's region), `sport_not_in_plan`, `market_not_in_plan` and `exchange_not_in_plan` (the scope's list for that product): the values accepted, sorted. `unknown_market`: the market keys this product carries, sorted (keyless `/v2/coverage`'s `markets`); a key another product carries may also be accepted on this route, and matches nothing here.

products.description: `unknown_market` only, when another product carries the market: those products, sorted, as the `{type}` of `/v2/odds/{type}` (or `raw`). Left out when no product carries it.

error.description: `insufficient_tokens`: the request's price is above the account's balance. Nothing was served or spent. The message names the price, the balance and the reset, and two fixes: add filters, or (plan `business`) talk to us about Enterprise at https://oddsrelay.io/contact, or (a custom plan) talk to us about raising your allowance at https://oddsrelay.io/contact, or (every other plan) upgrade. No `Retry-After`.

resets_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, whole seconds: when the pool resets; on a trial, the trial's end when that comes first.

quote.description: How to price a request for free.

upgrade_url.description: Where to upgrade. Absent on a custom plan (any plan code but `free`, `trial`, `trial_outreach`, `starter`, `pro` and `business`): it has no self-serve upgrade.

remaining.description: Tokens left, `unlimited`, or null when unknown.

last_seen.description: `{bookmaker key: {sport key base: ISO-8601 Z}}`: the last instant each venue and sport was read, the oldest observation behind the board, so `now - last_seen` is an upper bound on that venue's price age. The region's venues only, cut to a filtered body's venues and sports; always ISO; absent until the board carries the table; never on `format=bare`.

MatchedEvent.description: One fixture. Ids are opaque and the same on every route: one fixture is one id, and that id never changes for it.

event_id.description: The event's id: opaque, one per fixture, the same on every route, and never changed once served, whatever its exchanges, spellings or kick-off do next. An id found to name the same fixture as one served earlier is merged into it and listed in that event's `previous_ids`.

competition_key.description: The event's COMPETITION: one key per competition, the same on every route that serves the event, built from what its venues call it (`sports=<this key>` returns the competition whole). Shaped `<sport>_<name>`, so a sport base still prefixes it. Null when no venue's name for it identifies one competition, and on every racing event. Once served, a competition key never changes.

event_name.description: A team fixture that does not split into sides.

link.description: The venue's page for this event.

place_fraction.description: `each-way`, `extra-place`: the place terms as a fraction.

dutch_id.description: `dutching` only: 8 hex naming the dutch this leg belongs to. Group one market's offers by it and rate a dutch as 100 / sum(1/price).

lay.description: Lowest price first. An array of exchange offers; on `each-way` and `extra-place` an object `{win, place}` of two such arrays; absent on `dutching`.

available.description: Money available at that lay price.
Money available at that lay price.
Money available at that lay price.

RawOutcome.description: A bookmaker quote is `{name, price}`; a venue quoting a lay side is `{name, back_price, lay_price, available}` (`available` left out under `includeLiquidity=false`). No commission is applied.

id.description: The event's id: opaque, one per fixture, the same on every route, and never changed once served, whatever its exchanges, spellings or kick-off do next. An id found to name the same fixture as one served earlier is merged into it and listed in that event's `previous_ids`.

competition_key.description: The event's COMPETITION: one key per competition, the same on every route that serves the event, built from what its venues call it (`sports=<this key>` returns the competition whole). Shaped `<sport>_<name>`, so a sport base still prefixes it. Null when no venue's name for it identifies one competition, and on every racing event. Once served, a competition key never changes.

previous_ids.description: The ids that now resolve to this event: ids served for its fixture before they were found to be one fixture with it. Each still answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds`. Empty for nearly every event; never this event's own id.

last_update.description: The newest `last_update` of the venue's markets.

When this venue's market last changed (second precision): a price, a lay price or `available` moved, or a row appeared, including a venue's rows coming back after a few seconds off the board (see the Freshness note). A service restart can also move it once with nothing changed: dedupe on content. It is not a heartbeat: a quiet venue's `last_update` ages while the venue is still read (venue freshness is `last_seen` in keyed `/v2/coverage`).

processed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, or epoch seconds under `dateFormat=unix`.

total.description: Events matching the query, all pages.

processed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC, or epoch seconds under `dateFormat=unix`.

markets.description: Market keys seen under it on the matched boards.

competition_key.description: The competition this row's `key` belongs to: the row's own key for a competition's row, the competition an older key wholly belongs to, else null (a key several competitions share). Every competition on a board has a row whose `key` equals its `competition_key`.

id.description: The event's id: opaque, one per fixture, the same on every route, and never changed once served, whatever its exchanges, spellings or kick-off do next. An id found to name the same fixture as one served earlier is merged into it and listed in that event's `previous_ids`.

competition_key.description: The event's COMPETITION: one key per competition, the same on every route that serves the event, built from what its venues call it (`sports=<this key>` returns the competition whole). Shaped `<sport>_<name>`, so a sport base still prefixes it. Null when no venue's name for it identifies one competition, and on every racing event. Once served, a competition key never changes.

previous_ids.description: The ids that now resolve to this event: ids served for its fixture before they were found to be one fixture with it. Each still answers on `/v2/odds/event/{id}` and in `eventIds`. Empty for nearly every event; never this event's own id.

status.description: `degraded` when a board is past the age bound (`stale_boards`) or cannot be served (`missing_boards`). Still HTTP 200.

products.description: The products served in the region, in canonical order.

status.description: `live`: we are publishing odds for this venue and sport right now. `interrupted_24h`: we are not — no rows at this instant, or the venue's feed is interrupted now; it was publishing within the last 24 hours, which is why it is listed at all.

markets.description: Per product the region serves, the market keys it carries, sorted: each one a value that product's `markets` filter takes while this document is current (2up, each-way, extra-place and bog carry one each). A key under one product and not another is 400 `unknown_market` on the other's route when that route does not know it, naming the products that carry it in `products`.

CoverageKeyed.description: The keyed view: your key's products the region serves.

last_seen.description: The last instant this venue and sport was read (ISO-8601 Z); null when not known.
The last instant this venue and sport was read (ISO-8601 Z); null when not known.

resets_at.description: When the pool resets; on a trial, the trial's end when that comes first.

tokens.description: `remaining` and `limit` read `unlimited` on an unlimited account; null while the balance is unknown.

scope.description: Your account's scope, or null when it has none: `{"products": {<product>: {<axis>: [values] | null}}}`. A product not listed is not readable; within one, a null axis means every value. The axes are each product's filters: `sports`, `markets`, `bookmakers`, `exchanges` on the six matched boards; `sports`, `markets`, `bookmakers` (venues of both kinds) on `raw`, which also answers `/v2/odds/event/{id}`. Products and axes are always listed in that order and each list sorted. A value a call names outside it is a 403 `*_not_in_plan` with `valid`; a filter left out is trimmed to it.

scope_version.description: The version of `scope`, raised by each change; null when the account has no scope.

PriceTable.description: The price table the feed prices every call from, byte for byte. A call costs max(1, ceil(whole x each named filter's points / 100)).

BadRequest.description: 400: a parameter this route does not read or sent twice, a malformed value, gzip refused on standard, dutching or raw, or a filter value the catalogue does not know.
